result_text:
# Track 01 — FairFace Dataset Deep-Dive: Technical Profile

**For:** BiasAperture WP2 (`data_ingestion.py`) · **Stream:** A · **Prepared by:** Track 01 research pass
**Primary sources:** Kärkkäinen, K., & Joo, J. (2021). *FairFace: Face Attribute Dataset for Balanced Race, Gender, and Age for Bias Measurement and Mitigation.* WACV 2021, pp. 1548–1558 (arXiv:1908.04913) · [github.com/dchen236/FairFace](https://github.com/dchen236/FairFace) (inference fork, `predict.py`) · [github.com/joojs/fairface](https://github.com/joojs/fairface) (original release repo)

---

## 1. Exact CSV columns/dtypes — `dchen236/FairFace predict.py` output (race_7 variant)

Verified directly against `predict.py` source (function `predidct_age_gender_race`), not secondhand documentation. The script writes exactly these 9 columns, in this order, to `test_outputs.csv`:

| Column | Pandas dtype (as read from CSV) | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `face_name_align` | `object` (str) | Path to the *cropped/aligned face* written by the dlib detector step, e.g. `detected_faces/img001_face0.jpg` — **not** the original input image path |
| `race` | `object` (str) | One of the 7 race_7 labels (argmax of `race_scores_fair`) |
| `race4` | `object` (str) | One of the 4 race_4 labels: `White, Black, Asian, Indian` (argmax of `race_scores_fair_4`) — **extra column, not part of BiasAperture's locked schema; must be dropped or ignored at ingestion** |
| `gender` | `object` (str) | `Male` / `Female` |
| `age` | `object` (str) | One of the 9 locked age bins |
| `race_scores_fair` | `object` (str — **not numeric**) | Softmax confidence vector over the 7 race_7 classes |
| `race_scores_fair_4` | `object` (str) | Softmax vector over the 4 race_4 classes |
| `gender_scores_fair` | `object` (str) | Softmax vector over 2 gender classes |
| `age_scores_fair` | `object` (str) | Softmax vector over 9 age classes |

**Implementation gotcha (verified against a real sample row from `test_outputs.csv`):** the four `*_scores_fair*` columns are `numpy.ndarray.__str__()` output written into a CSV cell, e.g.:
```
"[6.7260742e-02 1.3291359e-05 2.1185173e-02 1.2533189e-02 5.9457081e-03 1.2895785e-02 8.8016617e-01]"
```
This is **space-separated, not comma-separated** — it is not valid JSON and `ast.literal_eval` will fail on it directly. `data_ingestion.py` needs a dedicated parser (e.g. `np.fromstring(s.strip('[]'), sep=' ')`) if confidence scores are ever consumed; `PredictionsFileInterface` as currently written only reads `race`/`gender`/`age`/`face_name_align` and is **not** touched by this, so this doesn't block M1, but will matter the moment confidence-weighted or SHAP-adjacent work reads these columns.

Column-name mapping already encoded in `model_interface.py`'s `_FAIRFACE_RACE_COL = "race"`, `_FAIRFACE_GENDER_COL = "gender"`, `_FAIRFACE_AGE_COL = "age"`, `_FAIRFACE_IMAGE_COL = "face_name_align"` is **correct** against this source.

---

## 2. Distribution across 7 race × 2 gender × 9 age bins

Official split sizes (train 86,744 / val 10,954) reproduced with full race×gender crosstab by Krishnapriya et al. (2020), *Understanding Fairness of Gender Classification Algorithms Across Gender-Race Groups*, arXiv:2009.11491, Table II — directly matches the FairFace repo's own released counts:

| Race | Female (train) | Male (train) | Total (train) | Female (val) | Male (val) | Total (val) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| White | 7,826 | 8,701 | 16,527 (19%) | 963 | 1,122 | 2,085 (19%) |
| Black | 6,137 | 6,096 | 12,233 (14%) | 757 | 799 | 1,556 (14%) |
| East Asian | 6,141 | 6,146 | 12,287 (14%) | 773 | 777 | 1,550 (14%) |
| Indian | 5,909 | 6,410 | 12,319 (14%) | 763 | 753 | 1,516 (14%) |
| Middle Eastern | 2,847 | 6,369 | 9,216 (11%) | 396 | 813 | 1,209 (11%) |
| Latino_Hispanic | 6,715 | 6,652 | 13,367 (16%) | 830 | 793 | 1,623 (15%) |
| Southeast Asian | 5,183 | 5,612 | 10,795 (13%) | 680 | 735 | 1,473 (13%) |
| **Total** | **40,758 (47%)** | **45,986 (53%)** | **86,744** | **5,162 (47%)** | **5,792 (53%)** | **10,954** |

Gender skews 53% male / 47% female train-wide, consistent across every race bucket (no race group deviates from that split by more than ~2 points) — race is well-balanced (9–19% per group, by design), gender is mildly and consistently imbalanced.

**Age-bin and full intersectional distribution:** the paper does not publish a per-age-bin table as clean as the race×gender one above. What *is* independently documented (Steinbach & Weber, *Assessing Intersectional Bias in Representations of Pre-Trained Image Recognition Models*, arXiv:2506.03664, using the 126-way race×age×gender crosstab of the train split) is that the intersectional cells are **highly imbalanced**, ranging **from 22 images** ("Middle Eastern, 70+, Female") **up to 2,972 images** ("White, 20–29, Female"). This is directly load-bearing for BiasAperture: a large fraction of the 126 intersectional cells will legitimately fall under `MIN_SUBGROUP_SAMPLE_SIZE = 30` and must be flagged `insufficient_sample=True`, not computed — this isn't a data-quality defect, it's the expected shape of the dataset when audits go past the 1-D race/gender/age level into intersectional subgroups.

---

## 3. Known label noise / annotation disagreement (from the original paper, §3.2)

The WACV paper describes — but does **not publish a single numeric inter-annotator-agreement percentage for** — its labeling pipeline:

1. **3 independent Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers** judged race/gender/age per face.
2. **Majority rule**: if 2 or 3 of the 3 workers agreed, that value became ground truth.
3. **No-majority re-annotation**: if all 3 workers gave different answers, the image was **re-published to a fresh batch of 3 workers**; if the second batch also failed to agree, the image was **discarded** (never labeled) — an explicit, silent filtering step upstream of the released CSVs.
4. **Model-assisted re-verification**: after step 1–3, the authors trained a classifier on the resulting (still "noisy," in their own words) annotations, ran it back over the full set, and **manually re-verified every image where the model's prediction disagreed with the crowd label**.

No quantified "X% inter-annotator agreement" figure appears in the accessible primary text. Two indirect quality signals exist, both worth citing but neither is a direct substitute for an agreement rate:

- **Independent replication**: Maluleke et al., *Studying Bias in GANs through the Lens of Race* (arXiv:2209.02836), re-annotated 1,000 random FairFace validation images via their own AMT pipeline and found **76% agreement** with the released FairFace race labels — this is a *third-party* re-annotation study, not a number reported by Kärkkäinen & Joo themselves; cite it as such.
- **Downstream benchmark accuracy** (Kärkkäinen & Joo's own trained race_7 classifier, as reported in later work citing the paper): race accuracy ≈93.7% on White vs. ≈75.4% on non-White groups, gender accuracy ≈94%, age-group accuracy ≈60%. This measures *classifier* accuracy against the label set, which is influenced by label noise but conflates it with genuine model error — treat as a loose upper bound on label reliability, not a clean noise estimate.

**Practical implication for BiasAperture:** treat FairFace race/age labels — especially age, given the ~60% own-benchmark accuracy ceiling — as **perceived/crowd-consensus labels with a non-trivial, unquantified error rate**, not ground truth in a strict sense. Worth a line in BiasAperture's limitations/scope-boundary section but does not require any schema change.

---

## 4. Train/val split sizes and `face_name_align` → file-path mapping

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Train split | 86,744 images |
| Validation split | 10,954 images |
| **Released train+val total** | **97,698 images** |
| Image resolution (both released padding variants) | 224×224 px |
| Padding variants released | `padding=0.25` (main experiments) and `padding=1.25` (commercial-API bias experiment) — same 86,744/10,954 split counts in both |
| License | CC BY 4.0 |

**⚠ Flag — headline-count discrepancy (not resolved here):** the paper's abstract and Table 1 both state the dataset "contains 108,501 images," and this figure is the one repeated everywhere in the literature, including in this project's own `CONTEXT.md`. The **actual publicly released train+val label files sum to 97,698**, not 108,501 — a gap of 10,803 images. This is a well-known inconsistency across secondary sources (several papers cite both numbers in the same paragraph without reconciling them). The most plausible read of §3.2 is that 108,501 is the count of faces *detected and sent to annotation* before the discard-on-no-majority step (§3) trimmed it down to the released set — but the paper does not say this explicitly, so this is an inference, not a confirmed fact. **This does not require a schema.py change** (the locked schema doesn't encode a total image count), but `CONTEXT.md`'s "108,501 images" line and any runtime/sizing assumptions built on it (e.g. the acceptance-criteria doc's "full FairFace (108,501 img) ≤ 4hr GPU" target) should be read as approximate, not exact, if `data_ingestion.py` ever asserts a literal row count.

**`face_name_align` vs. the dataset's native path column — these are two different things:**
- `face_name_align` is a `predict.py` **inference-time artifact**: the script crops/aligns whatever image was named in the input CSV's `img_path` column, saves it to `detected_faces/`, and writes that cropped-file path into `face_name_align`. It is generated fresh on every `predict.py` run and has no fixed relationship to the officially released dataset's directory layout.
- The **officially released label files** (`fairface_label_train.csv`, `fairface_label_val.csv`, distributed via the Google Drive links in the repo, not through `predict.py`) use a differently-named path column — commonly documented across FairFace-consuming codebases (Kaggle kernels, HuggingFace loaders, downstream repos) as `file`, with values like `train/1.jpg` / `val/1.jpg` relative to the unpacked image archive. I was not able to fetch these Drive-hosted CSVs directly (outside this environment's network allowlist) to confirm the exact header byte-for-byte, so treat `file` as strongly-corroborated-but-not-independently-verified-this-session.
- **Consequence for `data_ingestion.py`:** if WP2 ever ingests the *official* label CSVs directly (ground-truth demographic labels) rather than *only* `predict.py` inference output, it will need a **second** column-name mapping (`file` → `image_id`), separate from the `face_name_align` → `image_id` mapping `PredictionsFileInterface` already implements. `model_interface.py` as it stands only handles the `predict.py`-output shape; it does not yet handle the native label-file shape. Flagging this for Stream A rather than resolving it.

---

## 5. Edge cases: missing values, ambiguous labels, multi-label rows

| Edge case | Behavior / Finding |
|---|---|
| **Zero faces detected** | `detect_face()` in `predict.py` prints `"Sorry, there were no faces found in '{image_path}'"` and **`continue`s** — the image is silently **dropped**, producing **no row at all** in `test_outputs.csv`. This is a "row disappears," not a "row with nulls" failure mode — `data_ingestion.py` must reconcile input-CSV row count vs. output-CSV row count itself; `predict.py` gives no per-image success/failure flag. |
| **Multiple faces detected in one image** | Each detected face is cropped and saved separately (`{basename}_face0.{ext}`, `{basename}_face1.{ext}`, ...) and **each gets its own row** in the output CSV. One source image → 0..N `SubjectRecord`s. This is legitimate one-to-many *image*-to-*subject* mapping, not a multi-label row — each face still gets exactly one race/gender/age triple. |
| **Multi-label rows (a subject with >1 race/gender/age value)** | **None by construction.** Race, gender, and age are each single-label, mutually-exclusive categorical outputs (argmax over a softmax) — there is no mechanism in `predict.py` or the label schema for a face to carry two race labels. Real-world multiracial or gender-ambiguous subjects are still force-assigned to exactly one bucket by annotator/model judgment; this is a **taxonomy simplification**, not a data-format edge case `data_ingestion.py` needs to handle structurally. |
| **Missing/null demographic values** | Not possible in a syntactically valid `predict.py` output row — the argmax always resolves to exactly one of the fixed label strings. The only "missing" case is whole-row absence (zero-face images), not a null cell within an otherwise-present row. `model_interface.py`'s existing `if race not in RACE_LABELS: raise ValueError(...)` guard is correctly defensive against a *malformed/foreign* CSV, but will essentially never fire against genuine `predict.py` output. |
| **Ambiguous labels (ground-truth quality, not format)** | Covered in §3 — the discard-on-no-majority step means every row that survives to the released CSVs already cleared a 2-of-3 (or 3-of-3-on-retry) AMT consensus bar, but consensus ≠ correctness (see the 76% third-party re-agreement figure). No further structural ambiguity at the CSV-parsing level. |

---

## 6. Exact `predict.py` invocation and checkpoint file

**Setup (from the repo README, `dchen236/FairFace`):**
1. Clone/download the repo.
2. Install PyTorch and `dlib` (`pip install dlib`).
3. Download the pretrained model archive from the repo's linked Google Drive folder and unzip into a `fair_face_models/` directory alongside `predict.py`.
4. Download and unzip the dlib face-detection models (`mmod_human_face_detector.dat`, `shape_predictor_5_face_landmarks.dat`) into `dlib_models/`.
5. Prepare an input CSV with exactly one column, `img_path`, containing full paths to the images to be analyzed (template: `test_imgs.csv` in the repo).

**Command:**
```bash
python3 predict.py --csv "NAME_OF_CSV"
```
e.g. `python3 predict.py --csv test_imgs.csv`. Detected/cropped faces are written to `detected_faces/`; predictions are written to `test_outputs.csv` in the same directory as `predict.py`.

**⚠ Flag — checkpoint filename discrepancy (do not resolve silently; re-sync with schema owners):**

`CONTEXT.md`, `schema-lock-m1.md`, and `model_interface.py`'s docstring all name **`res34_fair_align_multi_7_20190809.pt`** as *the* race_7 checkpoint. Verified directly against the current `predict.py` source on `dchen236/FairFace` master, this is **not what the script actually loads**:

```python
model_fair_7.load_state_dict(torch.load('fair_face_models/fairface_alldata_20191111.pt'))
model_fair_4.load_state_dict(torch.load('fair_face_models/fairface_alldata_4race_20191111.pt'))
```

`res34_fair_align_multi_7_20190809.pt` only appears, **commented out**, as an alternate line in the sibling script `predict_bbox.py`:
```python
#model_fair_7.load_state_dict(torch.load('fair_face_models/res34_fair_align_multi_7_20190809.pt'))
```
Both filenames are real, both are linked from the `joojs/fairface` release page (Google Drive), and both are architecturally compatible (ResNet-34, 18-way output head = 7 race + 2 gender + 9 age). The most likely explanation is that `res34_fair_align_multi_7_20190809.pt` (Aug 2019, matches the arXiv v1 submission date) is the **original paper-release checkpoint**, and `fairface_alldata_20191111.pt` (Nov 2019, "alldata" suggesting train+val combined) is a **later checkpoint the maintainer swapped in as the active default** — but this is inferred from filenames/dates, not stated anywhere in the repo. Could not confirm whether the two checkpoints' predictions differ materially.

**This is a flag for whoever owns the WP2/schema sync, not a Track 01 decision:** BiasAperture's docs currently commit to a specific checkpoint filename that is not the one the reference inference script actually runs by default. Resolving it means picking one of: (a) update the docs to `fairface_alldata_20191111.pt` to match what `predict.py` actually does out of the box, (b) keep `res34_fair_align_multi_7_20190809.pt` and explicitly document swapping it in via the commented-out `predict_bbox.py` line, or (c) verify empirically whether the two checkpoints' predictions differ enough to matter for FR-003 metric computation. None of these are schema.py changes, but (a)/(b) touch `model_interface.py`'s docstring and `CONTEXT.md`/`schema-lock-m1.md`'s wording — out of scope for this research-only track.

---

## Summary of flags raised (not resolved) for the orchestrator / Stream A owner

1. **108,501 vs. 97,698** — `CONTEXT.md` cites the paper's headline "108,501 images," but the actually-released, ingestible train+val label files sum to 97,698. Any runtime/sizing target keyed to 108,501 is measuring against a number larger than what `data_ingestion.py` will ever actually see on disk.
2. **Checkpoint filename mismatch** — `res34_fair_align_multi_7_20190809.pt` (named in `CONTEXT.md` / `schema-lock-m1.md` / `model_interface.py`) is not the checkpoint `dchen236/FairFace`'s `predict.py` loads by default (`fairface_alldata_20191111.pt`). Needs a decision, not silent doc-drift.
3. **Two distinct "file path" columns** — `predict.py`'s output column `face_name_align` (inference artifact) is not the same thing as the official label CSVs' native path column (commonly `file`, unverified byte-for-byte this session). If Stream A ever ingests native label files instead of/alongside `predict.py` output, `model_interface.py` will need a second mapping, not currently present.
4. **Score-column parsing** — `race_scores_fair` and siblings are space-separated `numpy` array reprs, not valid JSON/CSV-native floats. Not a blocker for the current `PredictionsFileInterface`, but will need a dedicated parser once confidence scores or SHAP-adjacent work (Track 15/16) touches them.

*No changes proposed to `schema.py`, `RACE_LABELS`/`GENDER_LABELS`/`AGE_LABELS`, or `MIN_SUBGROUP_SAMPLE_SIZE` — the M1 lock is treated as ground truth throughout, per instructions.*
